lesson.text: A scatter plot shows pairs of data as points: hours practised and test score, for example.
Patterns: a positive association (both rise), a negative association (one rises as the other falls), or no clear pattern. Look for outliers, points far from the rest.
A line of fit runs close to the points. Its equation predicts values: y = 5x + 40 predicts 65 for x = 5.
A line of fit is only a guide: predictions far outside the data are less reliable.

exercises.prompt: Taller pupils tend to have bigger shoe sizes. What kind of association is this?
The more hours of TV, the lower the test score. What kind of association?
A line of fit can be used to make predictions.
A line of fit is y = 5x + 40. Predict y when x = 6.

choices: a point far from the rest
exercises.explain: A point far from the pattern.

exercises.prompt: Shoe size and favourite colour. What association would you expect?
A line of fit is y = 3x + 12. What x gives y = 42?
A line of fit for ages 5-12 predicts height at age 40. Why is this unreliable?
choices: It is far outside the data.
exercises.explain: People stop growing; the data don't cover 40.
